chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ali ibn Ismail, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ja'far ibn Imran, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Hajj and Umrah are two markets from the markets of the Hereafter. The one who is constant in performing them is under Allah's guarantee: if He keeps him alive, He will return him to his family, and if He causes him to die, He will enter him into Paradise.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of Hajj and Umrah as 'markets of the Hereafter'?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), Hajj and Umrah are metaphorically described as 'markets of the Hereafter,' highlighting the transactional nature of spiritual investment where the believer trades worldly efforts for eternal reward. The Imam emphasizes Allah's absolute guarantee (daman) for the pilgrim, ensuring that whether they return safely to provide for their dependents or pass away during the journey, their deed is fully accepted and they enter Paradise. This concept underscores the divine mercy that validates the pilgrim's intent and effort regardless of the outcome of their physical journey.
